items.title: Jerry Dodgion interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 9, 1996
items.q: we had one concert... Bob Brookmeyer sitting behind me... So we had everybody sit closer together... then the band started to sound better again

ctx.x: I wish I could have seen something at the Vanguard, just to see the band fit in there first of all. It must have been a little crowded.

Well we sat very close together and it was very funny that the first time we played out of the Vanguard we had one concert in someplace in Long Island at a college, I can’t remember which, and Monk had just played, Jackie McLean was playing with Monk and © Fillius Jazz Archive -4-

then we went on, and we were not sitting close together. And after the first — we played the first tune and Bob Brookmeyer sitting behind me I hear him say, “I told you you guys couldn’t play outside of the Vanguard. It sounds terrible.” So we had everybody sit closer together. So we sat closer together like we did at the Vanguard and then the band started to sound better again. It was really funny. It was great.
